Strategies for Enhancement in Food Production (Botany-II) · 2 marks

steps.label: Micropropagation
steps.margin_note: All three features: number, time, space.
lines: MICROPROPAGATION is the technique of producing
a LARGE NUMBER of plants in a VERY SHORT
TIME and in a LIMITED SPACE, using tissue
culture. It uses somatic embryos or small explants.
steps.why: Thousands of plants can be raised from one explant on a laboratory bench, which is what the micro in the name refers to.
common_mistakes: Saying micropropagation means growing small plants. It means propagating from small pieces, in quantity.
Leaving out the speed or the space. Both are part of the definition.
steps.memory_tip: Many plants, little time, little space.

steps.label: Somaclones
steps.margin_note: Definition plus the mitotic reason. Six lines.

lines.text: Somaclones are genetically IDENTICAL to the

lines: SOMACLONES are the plants grown through tissue
culture that are GENETICALLY IDENTICAL to the
They are identical because they arise by MITOSIS
from somatic tissue, with no fusion of gametes.
steps.why: Mitosis copies the genome exactly and no gametes are involved, so there is nothing in the process that could produce variation.
common_mistakes: Saying somaclones show variation. They are genetically IDENTICAL. (Somaclonal VARIATION is a separate, rarer phenomenon.)
Leaving out the reason. Mitosis with no gametes is why they are identical.
